Can Humans Compete with Artificial Intelligence?

A research essay on task automation, displacement, complementarity, and how work changes when software agents absorb more of the execution layer.

Abdul Wasea2026AI & society
Read manuscript on SSRN ↗Research repository ↗

Overview

Portfolio summary, not a verbatim abstract. Consult the manuscript for the full argument.

The question is not whether artificial intelligence will replace all human labor, but which classes of tasks are becoming software-shaped and how that changes the economics of work. This paper examines displacement pressure, productivity gains, and the continuing role of human judgment.

It argues that the most important distinction is not between humans and machines but between work that can be decomposed into repeatable procedures and work that remains socially, strategically, or ethically negotiated.

Key ideas

  • Distinguishes automation of tasks from elimination of whole jobs.
  • Examines complementarity between human oversight and machine execution.
  • Frames AI as a force multiplier that changes labor composition and bargaining power.
  • Emphasizes the uneven distribution of gains across industries and roles.
